kitty can be controlled from scripts or the shell prompt. You can open new windows, send arbitrary text input to any window, change the title of windows and tabs, etc.
Terminal graphics protocol: allows the program running in the terminal, hereafter called the client, to render arbitrary pixel (raster) graphics to the screen of the terminal emulator.

Shell integration with zsh, fish and bash enables features such as jumping to previous prompts in the scrollback, viewing the output of the last command in less, using the mouse to move the cursor while editing prompts, etc.

The ssh kitten allows you to login easily to remote hosts, and automatically setup the environment there to be as comfortable as your local shell; automatic shell integration, file transfer and reuse of connections, plus automatic forwarding of remote control sockets.

Control it from scripts or the shell; Extend with kittens using the Python language; Use startup sessions to specify working environments; Programmable tabs, splits and multiple layouts to manage windows.

Switched to Kitty from iTerm 2 on a work MacBook Pro and very impressed: snappy, easy to configure, works with a zsh/tmux setup after a few tweaks. Would like to drop tmux for kitty's sessions and multiplexing, but old habits die hard.

Best terminal I've found except for a deal-breaker: no bitmap font support, so it isn't comfortable on low-DPI monitors, and the author doesn't intend to add it. Using Termite instead until Alacritty is less buggy.
Switched to kitty a few months ago and it works REALLY well: very fast, with the best ligature support I've seen in a terminal. With FiraCode it makes code beautiful.
Gpu powered terminal emulator? This performs almost 100x worse than Mac OS Terminal.app. Cat-ting a long file takes 100x longer to draw on the screen!

After a month: slightly less usable out of the box than iTerm 2, and default shortcuts are counterintuitive (no Cmd-T/Cmd-W for tabs), but editing preferences is easy. Prefers it to iTerm because it's so fast and has ligatures (iTerm's Metal renderer lacks them). Maintainer responsive on GitHub.
This doesn't work on half of Nvidia-powered laptops (cites kitty issue #456).
Just tried kitty on MacOS -- Loved it. The diff and icat tools are must-haves. Won't use iTerm anymore.
Loves how user-friendly kitty's configuration is out of the box. But scrolling in vim misbehaves: some line backgrounds stay black until the cursor lands on that line or the screen is refreshed.
I tried it on MacOS (MBP retina) and damn, it renders text awfully.
Kitty is great; macOS Activity Monitor shows almost zero usage even during high-speed scrolling. Wishes there were a GUI configuration method, though that's not a big deal for a terminal.
I've used Kitty daily for years and it's brilliant. It just does the simple things really well and crazy fast. Can't really find fault.

macOS user: config took a minute to learn, but the docs are clear and it fits in a dotfiles repo. Favorite feature is auto layouts. Problem: TERM defaults to xterm-kitty, which broke nano on remote servers. Tabs look underwhelming next to native OS tabs.

Setting 'term xterm-256color' in kitty.conf is 'usable but i had a lot of issues. Copy pasty looses newlines, redraw issues in mutt, etc.' The author doesn't support using any TERM other than xterm-kitty.
Always found Kitty (or Alacritty) extremely laggy, plus it spins up the computer's fan; input lag around 300ms despite running at 60 FPS.
When you accidentally run tree on your whole ~/projects directory, kitty finishes in a fraction of a second, lag-free; even urxvt couldn't match that.

Switched to st because kitty's startup takes 5-10x as long (about half a second or more), noticeable when opening terminals often. A patched st has ligatures, and GPU rendering seems overkill for most use.
Used both st and kitty: kitty feels at least as fast as st, with infinitely more features and a proper configuration system.

Tested a dozen terminals: Kitty (and maybe Sakura) were the only ones that rendered a Unicode test file properly, with Alacritty second but quite broken. Alacritty has a noticeably faster startup time.

After 1 month: must transfer terminfo to every SSH server; double-click-drag selection wasn't normal; reopens fullscreen like last time; easy to set up default startup tabs, unlike gnome-terminal; CLI tools take different arguments in session files, barely documented. Still using it overall.
The kitty maintainer is 'bonkers rude'; his responses to privacy and security concerns (e.g. PR #3544 about update checks) made this user switch to wezterm/sakura/foot.
